title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
part: Night 61 · King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 430–433 (Night 61, continuing directly from nights-60), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition's Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor's slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 61 continues the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. Nuzhat al-Zamān, before the court, goes on with her first chapter on kingship, quoting advice and sayings of Khosrow, al-Manṣūr, ʿAbd al-Malik, ʿUmar and ʿAlī on the conduct of rulers, and verses on forbearance; then she turns to the chapter on good manners (adab) with a story of Muʿāwiya, his wife Maysūn and al-Aḥnaf ibn Qays. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الْحَادِيَةُ وَالسِّتُّونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-ḥādiyatu wa-al-sittūna
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the first and the sixty,
sentences.i: And when it was the sixty-first night,
sentences.n: الْحَادِيَة is the units-word of a compound ordinal: Arabic puts the unit first, "the first and the sixty", where English says "sixty-first".

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّ كِسْرَى كَتَبَ لِا بْنِهِ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna Kisrā kataba li-ibnihi
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the fortunate-one, that Kisrā wrote to his son:
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that Khosrow wrote to his son:
sentences.n: لِا بْنِهِ is printed as two pieces, لا and بنه; it is kept as printed. Read it as لِـ "to" + اِبْنِهِ "his son", with the alif of ابن stranded on the preposition. كِسْرَى is the Arabic form of the Persian royal title Khosrow (Chosroes). What follows is the king's letter of advice.

sentences.t: لَا تُوَسِّعَنَّ عَلَى جَيْشِكَ فَيَسْتَغْنُوا عَنْكَ وَلَا تُضَيِّقْ عَلَيْهِمْ فَيَضْجَرُوا مِنْكَ
sentences.tr: lā tuwassiʿanna ʿalā jayshika fa-yastaghnū ʿanka wa-lā tuḍayyiq ʿalayhim fa-yaḍjarū minka
sentences.l: Do not indeed widen upon your army, so that they do-without you; and do not narrow upon them, so that they grow-weary of you,
sentences.i: Do not be too lavish with your army, or they will do without you; and do not be too hard on them, or they will weary of you.
sentences.n: لَا + a verb is a prohibition; the ـنَّ on تُوَسِّعَنَّ is the emphatic nūn, "do not at all". وَسَّعَ عَلَى is "to be generous to" (lit. "to widen upon"), and ضَيَّقَ عَلَى is its opposite, "to be strict with". فَـ + subjunctive (فَيَسْتَغْنُوا, فَيَضْجَرُوا) gives the consequence: "so that they …", here "or else they will …".

sentences.t: وَأَعْطِهِمْ عَطَاءً قَصْدًا وَامْنَحْهُمْ مَنًّا جَمِيلًا وَوَسِّعْ عَلَيْهِمْ فِي الرَّخَاءِ وَلَا تُضَيِّقْ عَلَيْهِمْ فِي الشِّدَّةِ
sentences.tr: wa-aʿṭihim ʿaṭāʾan qaṣdan wa-imnaḥhum mannan jamīlan wa-wassiʿ ʿalayhim fī al-rakhāʾi wa-lā tuḍayyiq ʿalayhim fī al-shiddati
sentences.l: and give them a moderate gift, and bestow upon them a fair favour, and widen upon them in ease, and do not narrow upon them in hardship.
sentences.i: Give them a gift that is moderate and bestow on them a handsome favour; be generous to them in times of ease, and do not be harsh to them in times of hardship.
sentences.n: قَصْد is the middle course, neither stingy nor extravagant; عَطَاءً قَصْدًا is "a gift in measure".

sentences.t: وَرُوِيَ أَنَّ أَعْرَابِيًّا جَاءَ إِلَى الْمَنْصُورِ وَقَالَ لَهُ اجْعَلْ كَلْبَكَ يَتْبَعْكَ فَغَضِبَ الْمَنْصُورُ مِنَ الْأَعْرَابِيِّ لَمَّا سَمِعَ مِنْهُ هٰذَا الْكَلَامَ
sentences.tr: wa-ruwiya anna aʿrābiyyan jāʾa ilā al-Manṣūri wa-qāla lahu ijʿal kalbaka yatbaʿka fa-ghaḍiba al-Manṣūru mina al-aʿrābiyyi lammā samiʿa minhu hādhā al-kalāma
sentences.l: And it was related that a Bedouin came to al-Manṣūr and said to him: Make your dog follow you; and al-Manṣūr grew angry at the Bedouin when he heard from him this speech.
sentences.i: It is related that a Bedouin came to al-Manṣūr and said to him, "Make your dog follow you." Al-Manṣūr was enraged at the Bedouin when he heard such words from him.
sentences.n: The Bedouin does not explain his remark; the courtier's answer in the next sentence shows how it can be taken, that a follower goes where the bread is. يَتْبَعْكَ is jussive because it is the result of the command اجْعَلْ. الْمَنْصُور is the ʿAbbasid caliph al-Manṣūr.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ أَبُو الْعَبَّاسِ الطُّوسِيُّ أَخْشَى أَنْ يُلَوِّحَ لَهُ غَيْرُكَ بِرَغِيفٍ فَيَتْبَعَهُ وَيَتْرُكَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla Abū al-ʿAbbāsi al-Ṭūsiyyu akhshā an yulawwiḥa lahu ghayruka bi-raghīfin fa-yatbaʿahu wa-yatrukaka
sentences.l: And Abū al-ʿAbbās the-Ṭūsī said: I fear that someone-other-than-you may wave to him with a loaf, and he will follow him and leave you.
sentences.i: Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Ṭūsī said, "I fear that someone other than you may wave a loaf of bread at that dog, and it will follow him and leave you."
sentences.n: Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Ṭūsī is a courtier at al-Manṣūr's side. In the Arabic the dog is only "him"; the courtier takes the Bedouin's image as a warning that followers can be won away by whoever feeds them, so I have said "dog" to make the picture plain. The edition prints a shadda on يُلَوِّحَ, and it is kept.

sentences.t: فَسَكَنَ غَيْظُ الْمَنْصُورِ وَعَلِمَ أَنَّهَا كَلِمَةٌ لَا تُخْطِئُ وَأَمَرَ لِلْأَعْرَابِيِّ بِعَطِيَّةٍ
sentences.tr: fa-sakana ghayẓu al-Manṣūri wa-ʿalima annahā kalimatun lā tukhṭiʾu wa-amara li-al-aʿrābiyyi bi-ʿaṭiyyatin
sentences.l: And the rage of al-Manṣūr subsided, and he knew that it was a word that does not miss, and he commanded for the Bedouin with a gift.
sentences.i: Al-Manṣūr's anger subsided; he saw that it was a word that never misses its mark, and he ordered a gift for the Bedouin.
sentences.n: أَمَرَ لِـ فُلَانٍ بِـ كَذَا is "to order something for someone": لِـ names the receiver and بِـ the thing ordered. تُخْطِئُ keeps the ئ the edition prints.

sentences.t: وَاعْلَمْ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ أَنَّهُ كَتَبَ عَبْدُ الْمَلِكِ ابْنُ مَرْوَانَ لِأَخِيهِ عَبْدِ الْعَزِيزِ حِينَ وَجَّهَهُ إِلَى مِصْرَ
sentences.tr: wa-iʿlam ayyuhā al-maliku annahu kataba ʿAbdu al-Maliki ibnu Marwāna li-akhīhi ʿAbdi al-ʿAzīzi ḥīna wajjahahu ilā Miṣra
sentences.l: And know, O king, that he wrote, ʿAbd al-Malik son-of Marwān, to his brother ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz when he directed him to Egypt:
sentences.i: And know, O king, that ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān wrote to his brother ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, when he sent him to Egypt:
sentences.n: أَنَّهُ كَتَبَ … is a loose "that he wrote …" with the subject placed after the verb; the -hu anticipates the whole statement. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz was the caliph's brother and governor of Egypt. The edition prints a shadda on وَجَّهَهُ, and it is kept.

sentences.t: تَفَقَّدْ كُتَّابَكَ وَحُجَّا بَكَ فَإِنَّ الثَّابِتَ يُخْبِرُكَ عَنْهُ كُتَّابُكَ وَالتَّرْسِيمُ تُعَرِّفُكَ بِهِ حُجَّابُكَ وَالْخَارِجُ مِنْ عِنْدِكَ يُعَرِّفُكَ بِجَيْشِكَ
sentences.tr: tafaqqad kuttābaka wa-ḥujjābaka fa-inna al-thābita yukhbiruka ʿanhu kuttābuka wa-al-tarsīmu tuʿarrifuka bihi ḥujjābuka wa-al-khāriju min ʿindika yuʿarrifuka bi-jayshika
sentences.l: Inspect your scribes and your chamberlains; for the established-one, your scribes inform you about him; and the enrolment, your chamberlains make you know it; and the one-going-out from your presence makes you acquainted with your army.
sentences.i: Keep a close watch on your secretaries and your chamberlains. Of the man who is established in his post, your secretaries will tell you; of a new enrolment, your chamberlains will inform you; and the man who departs from your presence will make you acquainted with your army.
sentences.n: وَحُجَّا بَكَ is printed as two words; the final bā' of حُجَّاب has slipped onto the next word, so read "your chamberlains". The edition prints a shadda on كُتَّابَكَ, وَحُجَّا and تُعَرِّفُكَ, and they are kept; the later كُتَّابُكَ and حُجَّابُكَ are printed without it, and I have read them as the same plurals. وَالتَّرْسِيم is obscure: I take it as the registering or posting of men, which is the chamberlains' business, but the sense is uncertain.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ إِذَا اسْتَخْدَمَ خَادِمًا شَرَطَ عَلَيْهِ أَرْبَعَةَ شُرُوطٍ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna ʿUmaru ibnu al-Khaṭṭābi raḍiya Allāhu ʿanhu idhā istakhdama khādiman sharaṭa ʿalayhi arbaʿata shurūṭin
sentences.l: And ʿUmar son-of al-Khaṭṭāb, God was-pleased with him, was, when he took-into-service a servant, stipulating upon him four conditions:
sentences.i: Whenever ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may God be pleased with him, took a servant into his service, he laid four conditions upon him:
sentences.n: كَانَ + a perfect after إِذَا (here اسْتَخْدَمَ … شَرَطَ) describes a habit: "whenever he … he would …".

sentences.t: أَنْ لَا يَرْكَبَ الْبَرَاذِينَ وَأَنْ لَا يَلْبَسَ الثَّوْبَ الرَّقِيقَ وَأَنْ لَا يَأْكُلَ مِنَ الْفَيْءِ وَأَنْ لَا يُؤَخِّرَ الصَّلٰوةَ عَنْ وَقْتِهَا
sentences.tr: an lā yarkaba al-barādhīna wa-an lā yalbasa al-thawba al-raqīqa wa-an lā yaʾkula mina al-fayʾi wa-an lā yuʾakhkhira al-ṣalāta ʿan waqtihā
sentences.l: that he not ride the pack-horses, and that he not wear the thin garment, and that he not eat from the spoil, and that he not delay the prayer from its time.
sentences.i: that he should not ride heavy horses, nor wear fine, thin clothes, nor eat of the public revenue, nor put off the prayer beyond its time.
sentences.n: Each condition is أَنْ لَا + subjunctive, "that he not …". الْبَرَاذِين are heavy, non-Arab horses, a sign of show. الْفَيْء is revenue that came to the state without battle, here the public purse. يَأْكُلَ and يُؤَخِّرَ keep the hamza the edition prints.

sentences.t: وَقِيلَ لَا مَالَ أَجْوَدُ مِنَ الْعَقْلِ
sentences.tr: wa-qīla lā māla ajwadu mina al-ʿaqli
sentences.l: And it was said: There is no wealth better than the intellect;
sentences.i: It was said: There is no wealth better than a sound mind;
sentences.n: لَا مَالَ … is the "no … whatever" negation of a whole class. The same saying is usually quoted with أَعْوَد "more profitable"; the edition has أَجْوَد "better, more excellent", which gives good sense and is kept.

sentences.t: وَلَا عَقْلَ كَالتَّدْبِيرِ وَالْحَزْمِ
sentences.tr: wa-lā ʿaqla ka-al-tadbīri wa-al-ḥazmi
sentences.l: and no intellect like the planning and the resolve;
sentences.i: and no wit that equals foresight and resolve;
sentences.n: كَـ before a noun is "like, the equal of": here it names what an intellect is measured against.

sentences.t: وَلَا حَزْمَ كَالتَّقْوَى
sentences.tr: wa-lā ḥazma ka-al-taqwā
sentences.l: and no resolve like the god-fearing;
sentences.i: and no firmness like piety;

sentences.t: وَلَا قُرْبَةَ كَحُسْنِ الْخُلُقِ
sentences.tr: wa-lā qurbata ka-ḥusni al-khuluqi
sentences.l: and no nearness like the beauty-of the character;
sentences.i: and no act that brings one near to God like good character;
sentences.n: قُرْبَة is "nearness", and in religious speech any act that brings a person near to God.

sentences.t: وَلَا مِيزَانَ كَالْأَدَبِ
sentences.tr: wa-lā mīzāna ka-al-adabi
sentences.l: and no scale like the good-breeding;
sentences.i: and no scale of worth like good breeding;

sentences.t: وَلَا فَائِدَةَ كَالتَّوْفِيقِ
sentences.tr: wa-lā fāʾidata ka-al-tawfīqi
sentences.l: and no benefit like the granting-of-success.
sentences.i: and no gain like the success God grants.
sentences.n: تَوْفِيق is success or right guidance granted by God, a gift rather than something earned.

sentences.t: وَلَا تِجَارَةَ كَالْعَمَلِ الصَّالِحِ وَلَا رِبْحَ كَثَوَابِ اللَّهِ
sentences.tr: wa-lā tijārata ka-al-ʿamali al-ṣāliḥi wa-lā ribḥa ka-thawābi Allāhi
sentences.l: and no trade like the work, the righteous-one, and no profit like the reward of God
sentences.i: There is no traffic like righteous work, and no profit like the reward of God;
sentences.n: Your slice opens in the middle of a string of maxims. Each follows one pattern: lā + a noun in the fatḥa without tanwīn ("there is no …") + ka- "like" + noun. The speaker is still Nuzhat al-Zamān, addressing the king.

sentences.t: وَلَا وَرَعَ كَالْوُقُوفِ عِنْدَ حُدُودِ السُّنَّةِ وَلَا عِلْمَ كَالتَّفَكُّرِ
sentences.tr: wa-lā wariʿa ka-al-wuqūfi ʿinda ḥudūdi al-sunnati wa-lā ʿilma ka-al-tafakkuri
sentences.l: and no scrupulousness like the standing at the limits of the custom, and no knowledge like the reflecting
sentences.i: no piety like halting at the bounds of the Sunna, and no knowledge like reflection;

sentences.t: وَلَا عِبَادَةَ كَأَدَاءِ الْفَرَائِضِ وَلَا إِيمَانَ كَالْحَيَاءِ
sentences.tr: wa-lā ʿibādata ka-adāʾi al-farāʾiḍi wa-lā īmāna ka-al-ḥayāʾi
sentences.l: and no worship like the discharge of the obligations, and no faith like modesty
sentences.i: no worship like the discharge of the obligations, and no faith like modesty;

sentences.t: وَلَا حَسَبَ كَالتَّوَاضُعِ وَلَا شَرَفَ كَالْعِلْمِ
sentences.tr: wa-lā ḥasaba ka-al-tawāḍuʿi wa-lā sharafa ka-al-ʿilmi
sentences.l: and no merit-of-lineage like the humbleness, and no nobility like the knowledge
sentences.i: no lineage like humility, and no nobility like knowledge.

sentences.t: فَاحْفَظِ الرَّأْسَ وَمَا حَوَى وَالْبَطْنَ وَمَا وَعَى وَاذْكُرِ الْمَوْتَ وَالْبَلَاءَ
sentences.tr: fa-iḥfaẓi al-raʾsa wa-mā ḥawā wa-al-baṭna wa-mā waʿā wa-udhkuri al-mawta wa-al-balāʾa
sentences.l: So guard the head and what it has gathered, and the belly and what it has contained, and remember the death and the affliction
sentences.i: So guard the head and all it holds, and the belly and all it contains, and remember death and tribulation.
sentences.n: A proverbial warning, not a riddle: "the head and what it gathers" is the mind and senses (the tongue above all), "the belly and what it contains" is what you eat and drink. Guard both from sin.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ عَلِيٌّ كَرَّمَ اللَّهُ وَجْهَهُ اِتَّقُوا أَشْرَارَ النِّسَاءِ وَكُونُوا مِنْهُنَّ عَلَى حَذَرٍ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla ʿAliyyun karrama Allāhu wajhahu ittaqū ashrāra al-nisāʾi wa-kūnū minhunna ʿalā ḥadharin
sentences.l: And said ʿAlī, honoured God his face: Guard-against the evil-ones of the women, and be from them on caution
sentences.i: And ʿAlī, may God honour his face, said: Beware the wicked among women, and be on your guard against them,

sentences.t: وَلَا تُشَاوِرُوهُنَّ فِي أَمْرٍ وَلَا تُضَيِّقُوا عَلَيْهِنَّ فِي مَعْرُوفٍ حَتَّى لَا يَطْمَعْنَ فِى الْمَكْرِ
sentences.tr: wa-lā tushāwirūhunna fī amrin wa-lā tuḍayyiqū ʿalayhinna fī maʿrūfin ḥattā lā yaṭmaʿna fī al-makri
sentences.l: and do not consult them in a matter, and do not constrict upon them in a known-thing, until they not covet in the scheming
sentences.i: do not take counsel with them in any matter, and do not press them in what is customary and fair, lest they grow bold to scheme.
sentences.n: مَعْرُوف, "the known", is what custom and decency recognise as proper: the saying forbids both seeking their counsel and cramping them unreasonably. The ending of يَطْمَعْنَ (-na) is the feminine plural, which looks the same whatever the mood. Note too that فِى is printed with a dotless-looking ى, kept as printed.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ مَنْ تَرَكَ الِاقْتِصَادَ حَارَ عَقْلُهُ وَلَهُ آدَابٌ نَذْكُرُهَا إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla man taraka al-iqtiṣāda ḥāra ʿaqluhu wa-lahu ādābun nadhkuruhā in shāʾa Allāhu
sentences.l: And he said: Whoever left the moderation, his mind became bewildered; and for it are manners which we-mention them, if God willed
sentences.i: And he said: Whoever abandons moderation, his mind is thrown into confusion; and moderation has rules of conduct which we shall set out, God willing.
sentences.n: The printed text does not name the new speaker; I take it to be ʿAlī still. The perfect tense in a man-clause (taraka … ḥāra, "whoever left … became") is the normal Arabic way to say a general conditional.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ عُمَرُ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ النِّسَاءُ ثَلٰثَةٌ امْرَأَةٌ مُسْلِمَةٌ تَقِيَّةٌ وَدُودٌ وَلُودٌ تُعِينُ بَعْلَهَا عَلَى الدَّهْرِ وَلَا تُعِينُ الدَّهْرَ عَلَى بَعْلِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-qāla ʿUmaru raḍiya Allāhu ʿanhu al-nisāʾu thalāthatun imraʾatun muslimatun taqiyyatun wadūdun walūdun tuʿīnu baʿlahā ʿalā al-dahri wa-lā tuʿīnu al-dahra ʿalā baʿlihā
sentences.l: And said ʿUmar, was-pleased God with him: The women, three: a woman, Muslim, God-fearing, loving, child-bearing, who helps her husband against the time, and does not help the time against her husband
sentences.i: And ʿUmar, God be pleased with him, said: Women are of three kinds: a Muslim woman, devout, loving and fruitful, who helps her husband against the turns of fortune and does not help fortune against him;
sentences.n: ثلثة is printed with the long ā dropped, and I point it with the dagger alif (ثَلٰثَةٌ) so that it reads thalāthatun. وَدُود and وَلُود are masculine-form intensives used of a woman; such adjectives take no tā marbūṭa. الدَّهْر is time as fate, the blows of fortune.

sentences.t: وَأُخْرَى تُرَادُ لِلْوَلَدِ لَا تَزِيدُ عَلَى ذٰلِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-ukhrā turādu li-al-walad lā tazīdu ʿalā dhālika
sentences.l: and another, who is wanted for the child; she does not add upon that
sentences.i: another, wanted only for the sake of children, who offers nothing beyond that;
sentences.n: ذٰلِك is printed ذلك, with the long ā dropped, so it takes the dagger alif.

sentences.t: وَأُخْرَى غِلٌّ يَجْعَلُهَا اللَّهُ فِي عُنُقِ مَنْ يَشَاءُ
sentences.tr: wa-ukhrā ghullun yajʿaluhā Allāhu fī ʿunuqi man yashāʾu
sentences.l: and another, a shackle: God makes her in the neck of whom he wills
sentences.i: and another, a shackle that God hangs about the neck of whomever he pleases.
sentences.n: The shackle (غِلّ) is the iron collar of a prisoner. The shadda on غلّ is in the print and is kept in place.

sentences.t: وَالرِّجَالُ أَيْضًا ثَلٰثَةٌ رَجُلٌ عَاقِلٌ إِذَا أَقْبَلَ عَلَى رَأْيِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-al-rijālu aydan thalāthatun rajulun ʿāqilun idhā aqbala ʿalā raʾyihi
sentences.l: and the men also three: a man, sensible, when he turned-toward upon his opinion
sentences.i: And men, too, are of three kinds: one of sound sense, who, when he turns to his own judgment,
sentences.n: The sentence trails off here: the result of "when he turns to his own opinion" is left for you to supply (he is sufficient to himself and acts on it). Then the next type is set against him.

sentences.t: وَآخَرُ أَعْقَلُ مِنْهُ وَهُوَ مَنْ إِذَا نَزَلَ بِهِ الْأَمْرُ لَا يَعْرِفُ عَانِبَتَهُ فَيَأْتِي ذَوِى الرَّأْىِ فَيَنْزِلُ عِنْدَ آرَائِهِمْ
sentences.tr: wa-ākharu aʿqalu minhu wa-huwa man idhā nazala bihi al-amru lā yaʿrifu ʿānibatahu fa-yaʾtī dhawī al-raʾyi fa-yanzilu ʿinda ārāʾihim
sentences.l: and another, more sensible than he, and he is who, when the matter descended with him, does not know its ʿānibatahu, so comes to the possessors-of-opinion, and descends at their opinions
sentences.i: another wiser than he: one who, when some matter befalls him and he cannot see how it will end, goes to the men of judgment and yields to their counsel;
sentences.n: عانبته is printed so; it is probably a slip for عاقبته (ʿāqibatahu), "its outcome", and I point the letters as they stand. Literally فَيَنْزِلُ عِنْدَ is "he alights at" their opinions, an idiom for deferring to them.

sentences.t: وَآخَرُ حَائِرٌ لَا يَعْلَمُ رُشْدًا وَلَا يُطِيعُ مُرْشِدًا
sentences.tr: wa-ākharu ḥāʾirun lā yaʿlamu rushdan wa-lā yuṭīʿu murshidan
sentences.l: and another, bewildered, who does not know right-guidance and does not obey a guide
sentences.i: and another, bewildered, who knows no right course and heeds no guide.

sentences.t: وَالْعَدْلُ لَابُدَّ مِنْهُ فِي كُلِّ الْأَشْيَاءِ حَتَّى إِنَّ الْجَوَارِيَ يَحْتَجْنَ إِلَى الْعَدْلِ
sentences.tr: wa-al-ʿadlu lābuddā minhu fī kulli al-ashyāʾi ḥattā inna al-jawāriya yaḥtajna ilā al-ʿadli
sentences.l: and the justice, no-escape from it in all the things, even that the girls need to the justice
sentences.i: And justice is indispensable in everything, so much so that even slave-girls have need of it;
sentences.n: لَابُدَّ (lā budda minhu, "there is no escape from it") is printed as one word; I keep it fused and point it as the phrase it is. جَوَارٍ is the plural of جَارِيَة, a girl or slave-girl; here it is accusative after inna, so it ends in -a.

sentences.t: وَضَرَبُوا لِذٰلِكَ مَثَلًا فِي قُطَّاعِ الطَّرِيقِ الْمُقِيمِينَ عَلَى ظُلْمِ النَّاسِ فَإِنَّهُمْ لَوْ لَمْ يَتَنَا صَفُوا فِيمَا بَيْنَهُمْ وَيَسْتَعْمِلُوا الْوَاجِبَ فِيمَا يَقْسِمُونَهُ لَاخْتَلَّ نِظَامُهُمْ
sentences.tr: wa-ḍarabū li-dhālika mathalan fī quṭṭāʿi al-ṭarīqi al-muqīmīna ʿalā ẓulmi al-nāsi fa-innahum law lam yatanā ṣafū fīmā baynahum wa-yastaʿmilū al-wājiba fīmā yaqsimūnahu la-ikhtalla niẓāmuhum
sentences.l: and they struck for that a likeness in the cutters-of-the-road, the persisting-ones upon the wronging of the people; for indeed they, if they had not dealt-equitably (yatanā ṣafū) among themselves, and used the obligatory in what they divide, then their order would be-disordered
sentences.i: And for this they have given an illustration: highway robbers, who persist in oppressing people. Even they, did they not deal fairly among themselves and observe what is due in what they share out, would see their order fall to pieces.
sentences.n: يتنا صفوا is printed as two words; it is يَتَنَاصَفُوا, from تَنَاصَفَ "to deal fairly with one another", and I point the two pieces as printed. ضَرَبَ مَثَلًا, "to strike a likeness", is the idiom for giving an illustration. لَوْ … لَـ: the لَـ on لَاخْتَلَّ introduces the result clause.

sentences.t: وَبِالْجُمْلَةِ فَسَيِّدُ مَكَارِمِ الْأَخْلَاقِ الْكَرَمُ وَحُسْنُ الْخُلُقِ
sentences.tr: wa-bi-al-jumlati fa-sayyidu makārimi al-akhlāqi al-karamu wa-ḥusnu al-khuluqi
sentences.l: And in-the-sum, so the master of the nobilities of the characters is the generosity, and the goodness of the character.
sentences.i: In short, the chief of all noble traits is generosity and a good nature.
sentences.n: الْخُلُق (khuluq), "character", is the inner disposition; الْأَخْلَاق is its plural, "the traits of character". حُسْنُ الْخُلُقِ, "good character", is a stock phrase for kindly manners.

sentences.t: وَمَا أَحْسَنَ قَوْلَ الشَّاعِرِ
sentences.tr: wa-mā aḥsana qawla al-shāʿiri
sentences.l: And how-fine (is) the saying of the poet!
sentences.i: And how fine are the poet's words:
sentences.n: مَا أَحْسَنَ is the exclamation "how fine!"; what is praised (قَوْلَ) follows in the accusative.

sentences.t: بِبَذْلٍ وَحِلْمٍ سَادَ فِي قَوْمِهِ الْفَتَى * وَكَوْنُكَ إِيَّاهُ عَلَيْكَ يَسِيرُ
sentences.tr: bi-badhlin wa-ḥilmin sāda fī qawmihi al-fatā * wa-kawnuka iyyāhu ʿalayka yasīru
sentences.l: By giving and forbearance the youth became chief among his people, * and your being him is, upon you, easy.
sentences.i: Through generosity and forbearance a young man comes to lead his people; and for you, to be such a man is easy.
sentences.n: The edition prints this verse pointed, and the pointing is copied as printed. إِيَّاهُ, "him", stands for the thing one is, here "such a chief": "your being that".

sentences.t: وَقَالَ الْآخَرُ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla al-ākharu
sentences.l: And said the other:
sentences.i: And another poet said:

sentences.t:
فَفِي الْحِلْمِ اِنْقَانٌ وَفِي الْعَفْوِ هَيْبَةٌ * وَفِي الصِّدْقِ مَنْجَاةٌ لِمَنْ كَانَ صَادِقًا
وَمَنْ يَلْتَمِسْ حُسْنَ الثَّنَاءِ بِمَالِهِ * يَكُنْ بِالنَّدَى فِي حَلْبَةِ الْمَجْدِ سَابِقًا
sentences.tr:
fa-fī al-ḥilmi inqānun wa-fī al-ʿafwi haybatun * wa-fī al-ṣidqi manjātun li-man kāna ṣādiqan
wa-man yaltamis ḥusna al-thanāʾi bi-mālihi * yakun bi-al-nadā fī ḥalbati al-majdi sābiqan
sentences.l:
So in the forbearance is inqān, and in the pardon is awe, * and in the truthfulness is a means-of-rescue for whoever has been truthful;
and whoever seeks the goodness of the praise with his wealth, * will be, through the bounty, in the racecourse of the glory a front-runner.
sentences.i: In forbearance lies soundness, in pardon awe, and in truthfulness deliverance for whoever is truthful. Whoever seeks fair renown through his wealth will, by his bounty, take the lead on the racecourse of glory.
sentences.n: Printed pointed and copied as printed. اِنْقَانٌ is as the print has it; it is probably a slip for اِتْقَان, "soundness", and is glossed so. The second couplet pictures generosity as a horse-race, حَلْبَةُ الْمَجْدِ, with the generous man out in front.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ نُزْهَةَ الزَّمَانِ تَكَلَّمَتْ فِي سِيَاسَةِ الْمُلُوكِ حَتَّى قَالَ الْحَاضِرُونَ
sentences.tr: thumma inna Nuzhata al-zamāni takallamat fī siyāsati al-mulūki ḥattā qāla al-ḥāḍirūna
sentences.l: Then indeed Nuzhat al-Zamān spoke on the governing of the kings, until the present-ones said:
sentences.i: Then Nuzhat al-Zamān went on speaking of the statecraft of kings, until those present said:

sentences.t: مَا رَأَيْنَا أَحَدً اتَكَلَّمَ فِي بَابِ السِّيَاسَةِ مِثْلَ هَٰذِهِ الْجَارِيَةِ فَلَعَلَّهَا تُسْمِعُنَا شَيْأً مِنْ غَيْرِ هَٰذَا الْبَابِ
sentences.tr: mā raʾaynā aḥadan takallama fī bābi al-siyāsati mithla hādhihi al-jāriyati fa-laʿallahā tusmiʿunā shayʾan min ghayri hādhā al-bābi
sentences.l: Not we-saw anyone spoke in the field of the statecraft like this slave-girl; so perhaps she will make-us-hear something from other-than this field.
sentences.i: We have never seen anyone speak on statecraft as well as this girl does. Perhaps she will let us hear something outside this field.
sentences.n: In the print the alif of the tanwīn of أَحَدً has slipped onto the next word, so أَحَدً اتَكَلَّمَ is read "anyone … spoke" (أَحَدًا تَكَلَّمَ). بَاب, "door", also means a "chapter" or "field" of knowledge; the girl is about to move from the field of statecraft to the field of adab.

sentences.t: فَسَمِعَتْ نُزْهَةُ الزَّمَانِ مَا قَالُوهُ وَفَهِمَتْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-samiʿat Nuzhatu al-zamāni mā qālūhu wa-fahimat-hu
sentences.l: And Nuzhat al-Zamān heard what they had said, and understood it.
sentences.i: Nuzhat al-Zamān heard what they said and understood it.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ وَأَمَّا بَابُ الْأَدَبِ فَإِنَّهُ وَاسِعُ الْمَجَالِ لِأَنَّهُ مَجْمَعُ الْكَمَالِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat wa-ammā bābu al-adabi fa-innahu wāsiʿu al-majāli li-annahu majmaʿu al-kamāli
sentences.l: And she said: And as-for the field of the refinement, then indeed it is wide of the range, because it is the meeting-place of the perfection.
sentences.i: She said: As for the realm of good breeding and letters, it is of vast range, for in it every perfection meets.
sentences.n: أَدَب is not just "manners": it covers courtesy, polite learning, poetry and anecdote, which is what Nuzhat al-Zamān now offers. وَاسِعُ الْمَجَالِ, "wide of range", is an adjective followed by the thing it is wide in.

sentences.t: فَقَدِ اتَّفَقَ أَنَّهُ دَخَلَ رَجُلٌ عَلَى مُعَٰوِيَةَ مِنْ نُدَمَائِهِ فَذَكَرَ أَهْلَ الْعِرَاقِ وَحُسْنَ رَأْيِهِمْ وَزَوْجَتُهُ مَيْسُونُ أُمُّ يَزِيدَ تَسْمَعُ كَلَامَهُمَا
sentences.tr: fa-qadi ttafaqa annahu dakhala rajulun ʿalā Muʿāwiyata min nudamāʾihi fa-dhakara ahla al-ʿirāqi wa-ḥusna raʾyihim wa-zawjatuhu Maysūnu ummu Yazīda tasmaʿu kalāmahumā
sentences.l: So it has-indeed happened that a man entered upon Muʿāwiya, of his boon-companions, and mentioned the people of the Iraq and the goodness of their opinion, while his wife Maysūn, mother of Yazīd, was hearing the speech of the two.
sentences.i: Now it happened that one of Muʿāwiya's boon companions came in to him and spoke of the people of Iraq and the soundness of their judgment, while his wife Maysūn, the mother of Yazīd, listened to the two men's talk.
sentences.n: The print spells the caliph's name مُعَوِيَةَ, without the alif of Muʿāwiya; the letters are kept and the dagger alif supplies the long vowel. Maysūn, Muʿāwiya's wife, was the mother of his son and heir Yazīd. تَسْمَعُ كَلَامَهُمَا is a circumstantial clause, "while she heard the two of them".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا انْصَرَفَ قَالَتْ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أُحِبُّ أَنْ تَأْذَنَ لِلْقَوْمِ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْعِرَاقِ بِالدُّخُولِ عَلَيْكَ لِيَتَحَدَّثُوا مَعَكَ فَأَسْمَعَ حَدِيثَهُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā inṣarafa qālat yā amīra al-muʾminīna uḥibbu an taʾdhana li-al-qawmi min ahli al-ʿirāqi bi-al-dukhūli ʿalayka li-yataḥaddathū maʿaka fa-asmaʿa ḥadīthahum
sentences.l: And when he went-away she said: O commander of the believers, I love that you permit, to the people from the people of the Iraq, the entering upon you, that they converse with you, so that I hear their talk.
sentences.i: When the man had gone, she said: "Commander of the Faithful, I should like you to give the men of Iraq leave to come in to you and talk with you, so that I may hear what they say."
sentences.n: أَذِنَ لِـ… بِـ… is "to give someone leave for something": the person takes لِـ, the thing allowed takes بِـ (here بِالدُّخُولِ, "to enter"). دَخَلَ عَلَى and الدُّخُولُ عَلَى mean "to go in to someone", into his presence.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ مُعَٰوِيَةُ اُنْظُرُوا مَنْ بِالْبَابِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla Muʿāwiyatu unẓurū man bi-al-bābi
sentences.l: And Muʿāwiya said: Look who (is) at the door.
sentences.i: Muʿāwiya said, "See who is at the door."

sentences.t: فَقَالُوا بَنُوا تَمِيمٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qālū banū tamīmin
sentences.l: And they said: the sons-of Tamīm.
sentences.i: "The Banū Tamīm," they answered.
sentences.n: The alif after the waw of بَنُوا is a scribal habit: a final plural waw is often written with an alif, as in a verb ending (قَالُوا), even where the word is a noun. The vocalisation reads it as the ordinary banū.

sentences.t: قَالَ لِيَدْخُلُوا
sentences.tr: qāla li-yadkhulū
sentences.l: He said: Let them enter.
sentences.i: He said, "Let them come in."

sentences.t: فَدَخَلُوا وَمَعَهُمُ الْأَحْنَفُ بْنُ قَيْسٍ
sentences.tr: fa-dakhalū wa-maʿahumu al-Aḥnafu ibnu Qaysin
sentences.l: And they entered, and with them al-Aḥnaf son-of Qays.
sentences.i: So they went in, and with them al-Aḥnaf ibn Qays.
sentences.n: Al-Aḥnaf ibn Qays was the chief of Tamīm at Basra, remembered above all for his forbearance (حِلْم), which is why the poet's lines on forbearance stand just before his entry.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ مُعَٰوِيَةُ اِتَرِبْ مِنِّي يَا أَبَا بَحْرٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu Muʿāwiyatu itarib minnī yā abā baḥrin
sentences.l: And Muʿāwiya said to him: Draw-near from me, O father-of Baḥr.
sentences.i: Muʿāwiya said to him, "Come closer to me, Abū Baḥr."
sentences.n: The print has اترب. The sense, "come near", is certain from what follows, and the form is most likely اِقْتَرِبْ with its qāf lost; the pointing here follows that reading. Abū Baḥr, "father of the sea", is al-Aḥnaf's by-name (kunya).

sentences.t: وَضُرِبَ بَيْنَهُمَا سِتْرٌ بِحَيْثُ تَسْمَعُ كَلَامَهُمَا
sentences.tr: wa-ḍuriba baynahumā sitrun bi-ḥaythu tasmaʿu kalāmahumā
sentences.l: And there was struck between the two a curtain, in-where she hears the speech of the two.
sentences.i: A curtain was drawn between them, so placed that she could hear all they said.
sentences.n: The print has وضرب ("and he struck") with a nominative سِتْر, so a passive, "a curtain was drawn", is the evident sense and is how it is pointed. The two who are separated by the curtain are presumably Maysūn on one side and the men on the other; the dual هُمَا is loose, and the next clause has "the two" as Muʿāwiya and al-Aḥnaf.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ يَا أَبَا بَحْرٍ كَيْفَ رَأْيُكَ لِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla yā abā baḥrin kayfa raʾyuka lī
sentences.l: And he said: O father-of Baḥr, how (is) your opinion for me?
sentences.i: Then he said, "Abū Baḥr, what do you counsel for me?"
sentences.n: "How is your opinion for me?" is a plain request for advice, and the answer shows what kind: Muʿāwiya wants to know how he should keep himself.

sentences.t: قَالَ اُفْرُقِ الشَّعْرَ وَقُصَّ الشَّارِبَ وَقَلِّمِ الْأَظْفَارَ وَانْتِفِ الْإِبْطَ وَاحْلِقِ الْعَانَةَ وَأَدِمِ السِّوَاكَ فَإِنَّ فِيهِ اثْنَيْنِ وَسَبْعِينَ فَضِيلَةً وَغُسْلُ الْجُمْعَةِ كَفَّارَةٌ لِمَا بَيْنَ الْجُمْعَتَيْنِ
sentences.tr: qāla ufruqi al-shaʿra wa-quṣṣa al-shāriba wa-qallimi al-aẓfāra wa-intifi al-ibṭa wa-iḥliqi al-ʿānata wa-adimi al-siwāka fa-inna fīhi ithnayni wa-sabʿīna faḍīlatan wa-ghuslu al-jumʿati kaffāratun li-mā bayna al-jumʿatayni
sentences.l: He said: Part the hair, and cut the moustache, and pare the nails, and pluck the armpit, and shave the pubes, and keep-up the tooth-stick; for in it are two and seventy virtues; and the washing of the Friday is an expiation for what is between the two Fridays.
sentences.i: He said: "Part your hair, trim your moustache, pare your nails, pluck out the hair of your armpits, shave your pubic hair, and keep up the use of the tooth-stick, for it holds seventy-two virtues. And the Friday bath atones for whatever lies between one Friday and the next."
sentences.n: This is the list of the classical personal-care rules (the fiṭra): hair parted, moustache and nails trimmed, armpit hair plucked, pubic hair shaved, teeth cleaned with the siwāk, a bath on Fridays. In فَإِنَّ فِيهِ اثْنَيْنِ the accusative is correct: after inna, a fronted predicate (فِيهِ) leaves its noun accusative. The print writes وقلّم with its shadda; that mark is kept.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَ زَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahra Zāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahr Zād, and she fell silent from the speech the permitted.
sentences.i: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech unspoken.
sentences.n: The stock close of a night: morning overtakes Shahrazād and she stops the "permitted speech", the story she was allowed to tell. The print writes her name as two words, شَهْرَ زَادَ; it is kept so.
